title: Rotor-Twisted Clifford–Mandelbrot Sets: Breaking the Planar Reduction with Geometric Algebra
content: For a unit vector \(\vec{n}\) in a Euclidean space \(V\) and an exponent \(p > 1\), the Clifford--Mandelbrot set is generated by \(\vec{x} \mapsto (\vec{x} \diamond \vec{n})^p \diamond \vec{n} + \vec{c}\), where \(\diamond\) is the geometric product. This set is known to be a solid of revolution of a planar multibrot set, because the relevant orbits stay in the plane spanned by \(\vec{n}\) and \(\vec{c}\). We insert a rotor \(R\) and study \(T_{\vec{c}}(\vec{x}) = R \diamond (\vec{x} \diamond \vec{n})^p \diamond \vec{n} \diamond \widetilde{R} + \vec{c}\). The map is vector-valued, satisfies \(\|T_{\vec{c}}(\vec{x}) - \vec{c}\| = \|\vec{x}\|^p\), and its parameter set is compact and lies between two balls whose radii do not depend on the rotor. We characterise the rotations for which the planar reduction persists; for the half-turn about \(\vec{n}\), the set becomes the solid of revolution of the multicorn. For every other rotation of \(\mathbb{R}^3\) and \(p = 2\), the orbit of the origin leaves every plane for an open dense set of parameters of full measure; the proof combines a geometric-algebra argument with an exact Gröbner basis computation. We also determine the symmetries imposed by the rotor and give an explicit topological ball of parameters with attracting fixed points. Numerical experiments confirm the results and reveal boundaries in which smooth parts coexist with laminated structures.
